description: The `config` object of an enabled `response_size_limiting` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ResponseSizeLimitingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

ResponseSizeLimitingConfig.description:
Plugin: response_size_limiting — Per-proxy response body size limits.
Rejects oversized responses with HTTP 502 either via Content-Length
fast path (`after_proxy`) or after final buffering when
`require_buffered_check: true` is set (`on_final_response_body`).
`max_bytes` is additionally published to the proxy core as the effective
collection/streaming ceiling across H1/H2, H3, gRPC, retries,
coalescing, mesh mTLS, and HBONE: buffered collection aborts at this
route ceiling rather than retaining up to the larger global allowance,
and unknown-length streaming paths engage the frame-by-frame
`SizeLimitedStreamingResponse` adapter at this ceiling (known-length
paths reject an over-limit declaration before forwarding). Already-buffered
synthetic responses (mock, serverless, cache, federation, dedup replay)
are checked against the ceiling even when no plugin activated the
response body-hook gate, after any body transform. The effective bound
is the strictest active (nonzero) value of this limit and
FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES; a global limit of 0 means unlimited
and does not disable an active route limit, and multiple instances
compose to their minimum. It also bounds the buffered-representation
decode gate and compression admission.
Response-transformer output above this ceiling is a deterministic
gateway policy refusal: HTTP 502 with the Response body too large JSON error and limit,
X-Gateway-Error: overload, and error_class: dispatch_policy_rejected.
It emits one bounded warning. Oversized backend bodies retain backend
attribution; actual aggregate-buffer exhaustion remains HTTP 503.
Repeated identical Content-Length values are parsed per comma-folded
member and compared against the limit; a declared length that cannot be
reduced to one agreed value fails closed with HTTP 502. Bodyless
semantics (HEAD, 1xx, 204/205/304) are exempt from both checks.
Streaming rewrites are charged on the client-visible bytes: response
stream inspectors (every Forward, Terminate payload, and end-of-stream
flush), incremental gRPC-Web translation (base64 text expansion and the
generated trailer frame), and the gateway-generated mcp_gateway
aggregate SSE listener (greeting, events, keepalives) cannot deliver
more than the effective ceiling; the crossing frame is withheld and the
committed stream ends with a ResponseBodyTooLarge abort/reset.
Unknown keys and non-object configs are rejected. Explicit null
members are rejected; omitted keys keep defaults.

max_bytes.description: Maximum allowed response body size in bytes. Required and must be greater than zero — the gateway rejects plugin creation when missing or 0.

require_buffered_check.description: Force route-bounded whole-body buffering so the complete final post-transform size is proven before response headers are committed. Unknown-length streams are already bounded frame by frame when this is false. Enabling it adds memory overhead and rejects indefinite SSE streams whose complete size cannot be proven, including the gateway-generated mcp_gateway aggregate SSE listener (HTTP 502 before commit). An event stream whose backend declared one exact Content-Length within max_bytes (agreeing repeated members count as one), matching the pristine backend response, has proven its size and is admitted when no streaming response inspector on the route (for example an sse retry_ms prefix or an ai_* stream inspector) can rewrite its bytes.
